summary: Days after US and Israeli strikes on Iran began on 2026-02-28, Iran declared the strait closed and traffic largely halted. Ships from states Iran calls non-hostile may pass through Iranian waters, reportedly for a toll, and in May Iran set up a Persian Gulf Strait Authority to run transits. Start month is when PortWatch tanker transits fell, from 43.5 a day in February to 0.9 in March.

events.text: US and Israeli strikes on Iran begin.
Lloyd's List reports Iran running a "toll booth" system: ships pass after IRGC vetting unless their government has an agreement with Iran.
A US-Iran ceasefire halts major combat, but Iran keeps routing ships through its own waters and attacking those that don't comply.
The US begins a blockade of ships seeking to reach Iranian ports.
The US announces Project Freedom, a southern route that avoids Iranian waters.
With little done, Project Freedom is paused at Pakistan's request, to let ceasefire talks continue.
WTO data: since 28 February, crude carriers through the strait are down 95% and LNG carriers 99%.
The US and Iran sign a memorandum lifting the blockade, with safe passage for 60 days. Crossings rise for a while, not to pre-war levels.
Iranian attacks on ships off Oman on 7 and 8 July draw US airstrikes; Trump says the memorandum is no longer in force.
By early August the US has reimposed its naval blockade, after renewed Iranian attacks on shipping and Arab states.
Iranian forces say five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after mine strikes.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, hours after US forces disabled a cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman.

summary: On 2026-07-20 the Houthis (Ansarallah) declared a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, aimed at Saudi oil exports from Yanbu that had been running through the strait as Hormuz closed. CNBC reported a JMIC warning that the group had deployed missiles and drones near the strait, an EU naval mission advisory for ships linked to Israeli, US or Saudi interests to avoid the Red Sea, and Kpler data showing strait traffic down 34% the next day. On 2026-08-11 missiles struck the Egyptian-owned cargo ship Tihamah in the strait; Yemen's internationally recognised government blamed the Houthis and said at least six people were killed. PortWatch tanker transits averaged 11.6 a day in July and 8.5 in August.

summary: Underwater blasts ruptured both Nord Stream 1 pipes and one Nord Stream 2 pipe. Swedish and Danish seismic data showed two explosions; Denmark's prime minister said sabotage could not be ruled out. Reuters reported in March 2023 that the lines would be mothballed with no plan to repair them. On 14 October 2026 a former Ukrainian officer went on trial in Hamburg; German prosecutors accuse him of leading the operation for unidentified Ukrainian state entities. He and Ukraine's government deny involvement, and Russia denies blowing up the pipelines.

summary: QatarEnergy shut LNG production in early March 2026 after Iranian attacks and declared force majeure on its entire output. Missile strikes in mid-March damaged Trains 4 and 6 at this site, removing 12.8 million tonnes a year for three to five years, by QatarEnergy's estimate. With Hormuz restricted, Qatar's exports were about a third of pre-war levels in September, by Bloomberg's count, and under a quarter by Kpler's.

A drone incident briefly halted loading again on 8 September.
